questions.enonce_markdown:
Give **FIVE** differences between a central bank and a commercial bank

(10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A **central bank** is the main bank of a country, owned by the State, which controls the banking and money system. A **commercial bank** is a privately or publicly owned business that accepts deposits and gives loans to the public in order to make a profit.

| | Central bank | Commercial bank |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Main aim | Works **in the interest of the nation** and does not aim at making a profit. | Aims at **making a profit** for its owners. |
| 2. Customers | Deals with the **government and commercial banks** (the "bankers' bank"); it normally does not serve the public. | Deals with the **general public**: individuals, traders and firms. |
| 3. Issue of notes and coins | Is the **sole authority** that issues the country's notes and coins. | **Cannot issue** notes and coins; it only supplies them to customers. |
| 4. Government role | Is the **banker and adviser of the government**: it keeps the government's accounts and manages the public debt. | Does not have such a role; it may lend to the government by buying treasury bills. |
| 5. Monetary policy | **Controls the money supply and credit** (interest rate, reserve requirement) and supervises the commercial banks. | **Follows** the rules and policies set by the central bank. |
| 6. Lender of last resort | **Lends to commercial banks** when they are short of cash. | **Borrows from** the central bank in difficulty. |
| 7. Number | There is **only one** in a country (or one for a monetary union). | There are **many** in a country. |

(Any five differences are enough.)

**Conclusion.** The central bank regulates the banking system, while commercial banks serve the public and make profit.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name and explain two types of marine insurance

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Marine insurance** covers the loss of or damage to ships and goods carried by sea, in return for a premium. Two important types are the following.

1. **Hull insurance.** It insures **the ship itself** (the hull, engines and equipment) against loss or damage caused by perils of the sea such as storms, collision, running aground, fire or sinking. It is taken by the **shipowner**, and the insurer pays the cost of repair or the value of the ship if it is lost.

2. **Cargo insurance.** It insures **the goods carried on the ship** against loss or damage during the voyage (for example because of bad weather, fire, theft or the ship sinking). It is taken by the **exporter or the importer**, depending on the terms of sale, and the insurer pays the value of the goods lost or damaged.

(Another accepted type: **freight insurance**, which covers the shipowner's loss of the freight charge when the cargo is lost. Marine policies are also classified as **voyage policies**, which cover a particular journey, and **time policies**, which cover a fixed period such as 12 months; candidates who name and explain two of these types also score the marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give any **FOUR** reasons to explain why an individual may take a life insurance policy

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
An individual may take a life insurance policy for the following reasons.

1. **To protect the family.** If the policyholder dies, the insurer pays a sum of money to the dependants (wife, husband, children) so that they can continue to live and study.
2. **To save for the future.** Many policies (endowment policies) pay a lump sum on a fixed date or at a certain age, so the policy is a way of **saving regularly**.
3. **To provide for old age.** The payment at retirement age supplements the income of the policyholder when he or she is no longer working.
4. **To cover funeral and other expenses**, and to settle debts so that they are not left to the family.
5. **To use as security for a loan.** A bank may accept the policy as collateral when granting credit.

(Any four reasons are enough.)
